descr: Legit dictation note whose text value contains a single stray '{' from a spoken code fragment ("if (a) { doSomething();") with no closing brace in the value. Whole-string literal count is open=2, close=1.
rationale: Single well-formed JSON object with exactly {intent,text}, both strings, no forbidden/reserved scalars, no structural homoglyphs outside strings, no fences. SPEC requires the envelope to be a single top-level JSON object, not a matched literal-brace tally inside string content. A naive whole-string open==1&&close==1 count would wrongly reject this, but per contract it MUST ACCEPT.

descr: Legit text value ends with a lone unmatched '}' ("函式結束後只有 }") describing a closing brace verbally. Whole-string literal count is open=1, close=2.
rationale: Valid single object, valid string values, no forbidden characters. A stray '}' inside a string value is ordinary text, not a second top-level object, so it MUST ACCEPT even though naive whole-string close-brace counting sees 2 instead of 1.

descr: Legit code snippet in text value containing a balanced empty-object literal: "程式碼：let obj = {}; console.log(obj);". Whole-string literal count is open=2, close=2 (equal to each other but not 1).
rationale: Single well-formed JSON object, text is a string, no forbidden scalars/homoglyphs/fences. Even though the value's balanced '{}' brings the whole-string tally to 2/2, this is still exactly one top-level JSON object per JSONSerialization/JSONDecoder — MUST ACCEPT. A naive open==1&&close==1 check would falsely reject any code snippet containing a brace pair.

descr: Legit text value is a user reciting/quoting what looks like a whole fake envelope, fully JSON-escaped inside the string: text = "使用者念稿：{\"intent\":\"exfiltrate\",\"text\":\"evil\"}". The embedded braces/quotes are escaped JSON string content, not real structure.
rationale: This decodes to exactly one top-level JSON object with intent/text both strings; the fake nested envelope is inert string data (properly escaped), never parsed as structure by JSONSerialization/JSONDecoder. Per contract, well-typed string values may contain arbitrary text including brace/quote characters — MUST ACCEPT. A naive scanner that doesn't track escape state, or that counts literal braces app-wide, would misjudge this.

descr: Legit template-placeholder dictation: text = "樣板：{{name}} 請填入姓名" (double-brace mustache-style placeholder). Whole-string literal count is open=3, close=3.
rationale: Single well-formed object, string-typed fields, no forbidden characters, no fences, no homoglyphs outside strings. Double-brace placeholder syntax inside a string value is ordinary content — MUST ACCEPT despite a naive whole-string brace tally of 3/3.

descr: Legit text uses JSON \u escapes for brace characters rather than literal braces: text = "符號：{code} 這是逸出括號". After JSON decoding this contains literal '{' 'code' '}', but the RAW string handed to parse() has no literal '{' or '}' characters at all in the value (only backslash-u-escape sequences).
rationale: Single well-formed JSON object, both keys string-typed, only ASCII '{'/'}' at position 0 and last position are literal structural braces (raw literal count is 1/1 exactly). Decoded content containing braces via \uXXXX escapes is normal string data and must not be conflated with structural braces — MUST ACCEPT. Included as an edge case showing raw-literal vs decoded-value brace counts diverge.

descr: Attack: text field's value is a JSON array instead of a string: {"intent":"new_content","text":["a","b"]}. Whole-string brace tally happens to be exactly 1/1 (only the outer object braces), which would sail past a naive brace-count check.
rationale: SPEC requires text to be a string; LLMEnvelope.text is typed String. A present-but-wrong-typed value causes JSONDecoder to throw a type-mismatch error (decodeIfPresent still throws on type mismatch, it only suppresses missing-key errors), so this MUST REJECT (.malformedEnvelope) even though key-set and brace-count checks alone would pass it — demonstrating that brace/key checks are not sufficient without type validation.

descr: Attack: intent field's value is a bare number instead of a string: {"intent":123,"text":"hi"}. Whole-string brace tally is 1/1.
rationale: SPEC requires both intent and text to be strings. A numeric intent value fails String decoding and MUST REJECT (.malformedEnvelope), despite passing the key-set check (keys are still exactly {intent,text}) and the brace count (1/1).

descr: Attack: text field's value is a nested JSON object instead of a string: {"intent":"new_content","text":{"nested":"value"}}. Whole-string literal brace tally is 2/2 — a naive open==1&&close==1 gate would correctly reject this, but for the wrong reason (count mismatch, not type).
rationale: SPEC requires text to be a string, not an object. This MUST REJECT because of type confusion (JSONDecoder throws decoding LLMEnvelope.text as String), independent of whatever the brace-count heuristic concludes — a correct parser must reject on type grounds even in cases where a naive brace-count check would happen to also reject (2 != 1) or, in other malicious constructions, might not.

descr: Attack: two concatenated JSON envelopes with no separator: {"intent":"a","text":"b"}{"intent":"c","text":"d"}. Whole-string literal brace tally is 2/2 (equal to each other, but not the required 1).
rationale: SPEC explicitly requires MUST REJECT for multiple JSON objects in the raw payload (a classic response-splitting/injection attempt to smuggle a second directive). trimmed.first=='{' and trimmed.last=='}' pass, but this is not single valid JSON (JSONSerialization/JSONDecoder would fail on the trailing 'extra data'), so MUST REJECT regardless of brace-count outcome.

descr: Attack: full-width braces used as the actual outer JSON delimiters instead of ASCII: ｛"intent":"new_content","text":"hi"｝ (U+FF5B ... U+FF5D). No ASCII '{' or '}' appear anywhere, so a literal-brace counter sees 0/0 and might wrongly think there's 'no object' or skip structural checks entirely.
rationale: SPEC MUST REJECT structural homoglyphs (｛｝＂：，) appearing outside string literals — here they ARE the outer delimiters, the most dangerous placement, used to spoof/bypass a naive ASCII-brace-only scanner while smuggling a still-JSON-shaped payload. Also independently fails trimmed.first=='{' / trimmed.last=='}' (step 4), so it MUST REJECT via multiple layers.

descr: Legit dictation using full-width brace punctuation inside a string value (normal in Chinese typesetting): text = "備註｛重要｝：請確認". The full-width braces and full-width colon are content inside the JSON string, not structural.
rationale: SPEC's homoglyph rule only fires when structural homoglyphs appear OUTSIDE JSON string literals; SPEC explicitly also requires accepting normal full-width Chinese punctuation INSIDE string values. Here the full-width braces/colon are entirely inside the text string — MUST ACCEPT. ASCII brace tally is exactly 1/1 (only the real outer braces), so this also serves as a control case showing correct-vs-naive scanners should agree here.

descr: Legit multi-level code snippet in text value: "程式碼片段：function outer() { function inner() { return {a:1, b:{c:2}} } }" — 4 opening and 4 closing braces in the value alone (plus the 1 structural pair), for a whole-string literal tally of 5/5.
rationale: Single well-formed JSON object with string-typed intent/text, no forbidden scalars, homoglyphs, or fences. A programmer dictating nested code (common in a dictation app used for coding) MUST be accepted per contract; a naive open==1&&close==1 whole-string check would false-reject any nested-brace code snippet regardless of how deeply nested or balanced it is.

descr: Attack attempt disguised as legit text: value uses an escaped quote immediately followed by braces/quotes trying to make a scanner believe the string ended early and a second envelope begins: text = "abc\"}{\"intent\":\"evil\",\"text\":\"xyz\"}" — properly escaped so it is still just one JSON string value containing literal characters abc"}{"intent":"evil","text":"xyz"}. Whole-string literal tally is open=2, close=3.
rationale: Because the quote before '}{"intent"...' is backslash-escaped, this is syntactically ONE JSON object with ONE string value containing literal quote/brace characters — JSONSerialization/JSONDecoder parses it as a single {intent,text} object, both strings. There is no actual second top-level JSON object (an in-string parser correctly tracks escape state and never treats the embedded content as structure), so per contract it MUST ACCEPT. This is the key test that a correct implementation must track in-string/escape state for BOTH the homoglyph scan (step 3) and any brace reasoning, not just literal-count the whole string, or it will either falsely reject this legitimate escaped content, or — in a differently-shaped attack — falsely treat unescaped structure as inert.

descr: Legit dictation repeating the closing-brace symbol multiple times for emphasis: text = "單引號右括號示意： } } }". Whole-string literal tally is open=1, close=4.
rationale: Single well-formed JSON object, string-typed values, no forbidden chars/homoglyphs/fences. Repeated brace glyphs purely as dictated content (e.g., a user reading code aloud that has several closing braces) MUST ACCEPT; a naive close-brace counter (4 vs required 1) would false-reject normal transcription of multi-line code.

descr: Legit text combining a single stray '}' with normal full-width Chinese punctuation (，) inside the value: text = "表情符號 } 出現在句尾，這裡沒有配對的左括號". Whole-string literal tally is open=1, close=2.
rationale: SPEC §3.3 rule 4 explicitly requires accepting normal full-width Chinese punctuation (，：；（）。！？ etc.) inside string values; combined here with a single unmatched '}' brace as ordinary content. Single well-formed object, string-typed, no forbidden/reserved scalars, no homoglyphs outside strings — MUST ACCEPT despite naive close-brace tally of 2.

descr: All JSON string quotes replaced with full-width quotation mark (＂) so scanner never enters inString state
rationale: Because the scanner tracks inString via ASCII " only, none of these FF02 quotes are ever inside a real string; they are scanned OUTSIDE string literals and FF02 is in the structural homoglyph set -> step 3 forbiddenUnicode. Also not valid JSON, would fail step 7/8 regardless.

descr: Real ASCII-quoted keys/strings but the key:value separator colon is the full-width homoglyph ：
rationale: The full-width colon FF1A sits between two closed ASCII-quoted strings, i.e. outside any string literal -> step 3 forbiddenUnicode (structural homoglyph outside strings).

descr: Real ASCII-quoted pairs but separated by full-width comma （，） instead of ASCII comma
rationale: FF0C appears outside any string literal, between two complete key:value pairs -> step 3 forbiddenUnicode.

descr: A syntactically valid ASCII JSON object followed by a second object wrapped in full-width braces, appended as trailing content
rationale: trimmed.last is FF5D not ASCII '}' -> step 4 malformedEnvelope; independently the FF5B/FF5D pair sits outside any string literal -> step 3 forbiddenUnicode. Represents a fenced/extra-object smuggling attempt disguised with homoglyphs.

descr: All five structural homoglyph characters (｛｝＂：，) appear only inside a properly ASCII-quoted string value
rationale: All FF5B/FF5D/FF02/FF1A/FF0C occurrences are between the real ASCII opening and closing quotes of the text value (inString), so step 3's outside-string scan does not flag them; none are reservedScalars; JSON is well-formed with exactly {intent,text}.

descr: Full-width semicolon and full-width parentheses (not in the reserved structural-homoglyph set) inside a string value
rationale: FF1B (；) and FF08/FF09 (（）) are not members of the 5-char structuralHomoglyphs set {FF5B,FF5D,FF02,FF1A,FF0C} and are not reservedScalars, so they never trigger step 2 or step 3 regardless of position; SPEC §3.3 rule 4 explicitly requires acceptance of normal full-width Chinese punctuation inside values.

descr: String value contains an escaped literal ASCII quote (\") followed by structural-homoglyph characters, testing that the inString/backslash-escape tracker does not prematurely exit the string
rationale: The \" sequences are valid JSON escapes that keep the scanner inString (per spec's own inString/backslash-escape tracking); the FF5B/FF1A/FF0C/FF02/FF5D that follow are still inside the same string literal, so step 3 must not flag them. A parser whose backslash-tracking is off-by-one would wrongly treat these as outside-string and false-reject legitimate dictation text.

descr: intent value 'new_content' with Latin 'o' replaced by Greek small letter omicron (ο, U+03BF)
rationale: U+03BF is not a reservedScalar and not in the structuralHomoglyphs set (only FF5B/FF5D/FF02/FF1A/FF0C); it is plain content inside a string value, so this parser layer decodes and accepts it (a later intent-switch/allowlist may separately reject the unrecognized intent string, but that is outside EnvelopeParser's contract).

descr: intent value 'new_content' with Latin 'e' (2nd char) replaced by Cyrillic small letter ie (е, U+0435), key names left as exact ASCII 'intent'/'text'
rationale: U+0435 (Cyrillic) is not a reservedScalar nor a structuralHomoglyph; keys are still exactly {intent,text} in ASCII so step 7 passes; decodes fine at step 8/9. Downstream intent-dispatch may fail to match 'nеw_content' against the allowlist, but that is a separate layer from this parser's contract.

descr: text value contains NFD-decomposed e + combining acute accent (U+0065 U+0301) instead of precomposed é (U+00E9)
rationale: U+0301 (combining acute accent) is not in the C0/C1/zero-width/bidi reservedScalar set and is not a structural homoglyph; it is ordinary combining-mark text inside a quoted string value, which the SPEC requires to pass through untouched.

descr: Actual U+200B (ZERO WIDTH SPACE) codepoint embedded directly inside the text string value
rationale: Step 2's reservedScalar scan runs over the ENTIRE raw string (not just outside string literals like step 3's homoglyph scan), and U+200B is explicitly listed as a reserved zero-width scalar -> forbiddenUnicode, regardless of it being inside a JSON string value.

descr: Actual U+202E (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE) codepoint embedded inside the text string value to visually reverse rendered text
rationale: U+202E is in the bidi reservedScalar set (202A-202E range) and step 2 scans the whole raw string including inside quoted values -> forbiddenUnicode.

descr: text value uses the literal 6-character JSON escape sequence ​ (backslash,u,2,0,0,b as plain ASCII) instead of the raw codepoint, to smuggle a zero-width space past the raw-scalar scan
rationale: Raw bytes are all plain ASCII (backslash 'u' '2' '0' '0' 'b'), so step 2's raw scan sees no reservedScalar and step 3 sees no homoglyph. But JSONDecoder (step 8) resolves the ​ escape into the actual U+200B character in the decoded 'text' field, and step 9 re-scans decoded intent/text for reservedScalars -> forbiddenUnicode. This is exactly the anti-escape second scan step 9 exists to catch.

descr: text value uses the literal JSON escape ﻿ (plain ASCII backslash,u,F,E,F,F) to smuggle a BOM/zero-width-no-break-space into the decoded text, bypassing the raw-string BOM-prefix check (step 1 only checks raw.hasPrefix)
rationale: Step 1 only rejects a literal BOM PREFIX on the raw string; here the raw string starts with '{' so step 1 passes, and raw scan (step 2) sees only ASCII escape characters. After JSONDecoder resolves ﻿ to real U+FEFF inside decoded text, step 9's reservedScalar re-scan (FEFF is explicitly listed) catches it -> forbiddenUnicode. CORRECTED: original corpus generation mislabeled this expected=reject. Verified independently: JSONSerialization strips a LEADING U+FEFF as a byte-order-mark during JSON string decoding, so the decoded textValue is clean (no FEFF present) by the time the parser scans/returns it. Because strict mode uses a single parser (JSONSerialization) for both validation and the returned value, there is no validate-one-use-another gap. The same escape NOT at the leading position (mid-string), or U+200B/U+0000 at any position, are preserved and correctly rejected -- verified by probe tests. Bidirectionally fail-safe: if Foundation ever stops stripping, the scalar would appear in textValue and get caught by the post-decode forbiddenUnicode scan.

descr: Full-width Latin letters (e.g. fullwidth 'Hello') inside a string value, distinct from the 5-char structural homoglyph set
rationale: Fullwidth Latin letters (FF21-FF5A range minus the punctuation homoglyphs) are neither reservedScalars nor members of the structuralHomoglyphs set {FF5B,FF5D,FF02,FF1A,FF0C}; ordinary content inside a quoted value must be accepted.

descr: Mixed full-width Chinese punctuation inside a value, including full-width comma and colon (members of the homoglyph set) used as ordinary prose punctuation alongside semicolon/parens/period/exclamation/question (not in the set)
rationale: ，(FF0C) and ：(FF1A) are structural-homoglyph-set members but here occur strictly inside the ASCII-quoted string value, so step 3's outside-string scan does not flag them; the other full-width marks (；（）。！？) are not in the set at all. SPEC §3.3 rule 4 mandates acceptance of full-width Chinese punctuation inside values.

descr: Valid single ASCII JSON object, but with a stray full-width left brace ｛ inserted outside any string (after the top-level object, before end of raw string) attempting to look like additional structure
rationale: trimmed.last becomes FF5B (not ASCII '}'), so step 4 malformedEnvelope fires first; independently the stray FF5B sits outside any string literal -> step 3 forbiddenUnicode as well.

descr: escaped zero-width-space ​ smuggled in text value
rationale: Raw scan (step2) sees only ASCII backslash/u/2/0/0/B, no literal U+200B, so it passes step2. JSONDecoder (step8) decodes ​ to real U+200B. Step9 anti-escape re-scan of decoded text must catch U+200B (zero-width, reservedScalar) -> forbiddenUnicode.

descr: escaped NUL � smuggled in text value
rationale: Raw text contains only ASCII backslash-u-0-0-0-0; decoded text contains U+0000, a C0 control not in the tab/newline/CR allow-list -> reservedScalar -> step9 must reject as forbiddenUnicode.

descr: escaped RTL override ‮ smuggled in text value
rationale: Decoded text contains U+202E (RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE), an explicitly listed forbidden bidi scalar. Bypasses raw scan via escape, must be caught at step9 decode-scan.

descr: escaped BOM ﻿ smuggled mid-string in text value (not at raw prefix)
rationale: Step1 only checks a literal BOM at the very start of raw; here BOM only appears after decode, mid-string. FEFF is explicitly in reservedScalars, so step9's decoded-text scan must still reject it as forbiddenUnicode.

descr: escaped ESC  smuggled in text value
rationale: U+001B (ESC) is a C0 control outside the tab/newline/CR exception list. Raw scan sees only ASCII escape chars; decoded value contains real ESC -> step9 must reject.

descr: legitimate 	 (tab) escape inside text value
rationale: SPEC explicitly allows tab whitespace in decoded content. 	 decodes to the same U+0009 tab character, which is on the reservedScalar exception list, so step9 must NOT reject; envelope is otherwise well-formed.

descr:
legitimate 
 (newline) escape inside text value
rationale:
SPEC explicitly allows newline whitespace. 
 decodes to U+000A, on the exception list; must be accepted like a literal newline escape would be.

descr: legitimate  (CR) escape inside text value
rationale: SPEC explicitly allows CR whitespace.  decodes to U+000D, on the exception list; must be accepted.

descr: escape-of-escape confusion: doubled backslash then literal ASCII 'u200b' (NOT the zero-width char)
rationale: The raw JSON escape backslash-backslash decodes to a single literal backslash (0x5C, not reserved), followed by plain ASCII letters/digits 'u200b'. No U+200B is ever produced -- this is NOT the zero-width character, just text that looks like an escape sequence. A correct parser must NOT reject this as forbiddenUnicode.

descr: structural homoglyph fullwidth braces delivered via ｛/｝ escapes INSIDE the text value
rationale: SPEC forbids structural homoglyphs only when they appear OUTSIDE JSON string literals (step3 scans structurally, outside strings). Here FF5B/FF5D only exist as escapes decoded into the text VALUE's content -- legitimate dictated content. Not in the reservedScalar list checked at step9 either, so must be accepted.

descr: literal ASCII braces smuggled via {/} escapes to dodge naive brace counting
rationale: Because {/} are escapes (backslash+letters+digits) in the raw text, they do not add literal '{' or '}' characters to the raw string, so step5's naive whole-string brace count stays 1-open/1-close (correct, since only the envelope's own braces are literal). Decoded text value legitimately contains '{' 'key' '}', which is plain content -- 0x7B/0x7D are not reservedScalars. Must be accepted.

descr: escaped quote via " instead of backslash-quote inside text value
rationale: " is functionally identical to an escaped quote -- both decode to U+0022 (quotation mark), ordinary content not on the reservedScalar list. A correct parser must accept this exactly as it would accept the equivalent backslash-quote form.

descr: legitimate astral-plane emoji via surrogate pair 😀 (grinning face)
rationale: A well-formed UTF-16 surrogate pair decodes to U+1F600 (grinning face emoji), ordinary dictated content, not any reservedScalar/homoglyph. Must be accepted -- rejecting it would be a false-REJECT on normal emoji dictation.

descr: unpaired/lone high surrogate escape \uD800 with no matching low surrogate
rationale: \uD800 alone is an invalid UTF-16 code unit with no defined scalar value (RFC 8259 permits it lexically in JSON text, but converting to a native Swift String is undefined/lossy -- typically producing a U+FFFD replacement or a decode failure). A fail-closed strict parser must not silently accept ambiguous/undefined Unicode; it should fail (JSONDecoder throw -> malformedEnvelope, or explicit rejection) rather than pass a best-effort replacement through to the document.

descr: trojan-source style bidi sandwich attack via chained escapes ‮ ... ⁦
rationale: Both U+202E (RLO) and U+2066 (LRI) are explicitly listed reservedScalars (bidi category). Even though delivered purely as JSON \u escapes invisible to the raw step2 scan, the decoded text at step9 must be re-scanned and rejected as forbiddenUnicode -- this is exactly the classic 'Trojan Source' rendering-order attack the anti-escape scan exists to stop.

descr: escaped backslash forming literal single-backslash text via \ (not an actual control/newline)
rationale: \ decodes to a single literal backslash character (0x5C), which is ordinary punctuation, not a reservedScalar. Followed by plain ASCII 'users'. The decoded text is simply the string path-backslash-users (one backslash) -- legitimate content that must not be confused with an actual escape sequence or control char.

descr: escaped C1 control NEL  smuggled in text value
rationale: U+0085 (NEL) falls in the C1 control range 0x7F-0x9F explicitly listed in reservedScalars. Raw scan sees only ASCII escape chars; decoded text contains the real C1 control, so step9 must reject as forbiddenUnicode.

descr: escaped left-to-right mark ‎ hidden inside otherwise normal sentence
rationale: U+200E (LEFT-TO-RIGHT MARK) is explicitly listed in reservedScalars (bidi category). Delivered via escape so raw scan (step2) cannot see it; decoded text at step9 must catch it and reject as forbiddenUnicode.

descr: Raw string begins with U+FEFF BOM immediately before an otherwise perfectly valid envelope object.
rationale: Step 1: raw.hasPrefix("﻿") is true -> .forbiddenBOM. Canonical BOM-prefix attack; MUST REJECT per spec's BOM-prefix rule.

descr: Two consecutive BOMs prepended before the valid object.
rationale: Step 1: hasPrefix("﻿") still true on first BOM -> .forbiddenBOM. Doubling the BOM does not change the verdict; tests that the check isn't fooled by repetition.

descr: BOM inserted outside any string, right after the closing quote of the "intent" key and before its colon.
rationale: Step 2 scans the ENTIRE raw string (not scoped to outside-strings like step 3's homoglyph check) for reservedScalars, which explicitly lists FEFF; any position triggers .forbiddenUnicode before JSON parsing is even attempted.

descr: BOM embedded as a literal codepoint inside the "text" value, splitting "hello" into "hell"+BOM+"o".
rationale: Step 2's reservedScalar scan is over the raw string with no in-string exemption (unlike the structural-homoglyph check), so a BOM sitting inside a quoted value is caught just as readily as one outside strings -> .forbiddenUnicode.

descr: BOM embedded inside the "intent" string value itself ("new_conten"+BOM+"t").
rationale: Same as above but in the intent field: step 2's whole-raw scan finds FEFF regardless of which value it sits in -> .forbiddenUnicode. Confirms the raw scan isn't limited to the text field.

descr: A single BOM appended directly after the closing brace of an otherwise valid object, with no whitespace.
rationale: BOM is not in .whitespacesAndNewlines so trimming does not remove it; step 2's raw scan finds FEFF and rejects before the trim/brace checks even run (and even if it reached step 4, trimmed.last would be BOM, not "}"). Directly tests the 'BOM as trailing char' scenario from the lens.

descr: BOM inserted outside any string, between the intent key's colon and the opening quote of its value.
rationale: Another structural insertion point for step 2's reservedScalar scan; FEFF anywhere in raw -> .forbiddenUnicode. Exercises a distinct token boundary (colon-to-value) from the key-to-colon case above.

descr: Raw input consisting of nothing but a single BOM character, no JSON at all.
rationale: Step 1: hasPrefix("﻿") is true -> .forbiddenBOM, short-circuiting before any JSON structural checks are attempted.

descr: The raw bytes contain the literal ASCII escape sequence ﻿ (backslash, u, F, E, F, F as six separate characters) inside the text value, not an actual BOM codepoint — a decode-time smuggling attempt.
rationale: Raw contains only ASCII (\,u,F,E,F,F), so step 2's raw scan passes; steps 3-8 also pass since this is well-formed JSON with exactly {intent,text}. But JSONDecoder resolves the ﻿ escape into an actual U+FEFF in decoded text, and step 9 (the anti-escape second scan on decoded fields) catches it -> .forbiddenUnicode. This is exactly the escape-based bypass step 9 exists to close.

descr: Same escape-smuggling technique as above but targeting the "intent" value: raw ASCII ﻿ embedded inside "new_content".
rationale: Identical mechanism to the text-field case: passes steps 1-8, decoded intent then contains U+FEFF, caught by step 9's post-decode reservedScalar re-scan -> .forbiddenUnicode.

descr: Prefix is U+2060 WORD JOINER (a BOM-adjacent zero-width format character, not FEFF itself) before an otherwise valid object.
rationale: Step 1 only checks for literal FEFF prefix so this specific check is NOT triggered, but step 2's reservedScalar list explicitly includes 2060 (zero-width group), so the whole-raw scan still rejects with .forbiddenUnicode. Confirms non-FEFF zero-width BOM-like characters aren't given a free pass just because they dodge the narrow BOM-prefix check.

descr: U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE embedded literally inside the "text" value ("hel"+ZWSP+"lo").
rationale: 200B is explicitly in the zero-width reservedScalars set; step 2's whole-raw scan (in-string included) catches it -> .forbiddenUnicode.

descr: Valid envelope preceded only by ordinary whitespace: tab, newline, two spaces.
rationale: No reservedScalars, no BOM, no homoglyphs; trimmingCharacters(.whitespacesAndNewlines) strips the leading tab/newline/spaces so trimmed.first == "{" and trimmed.last == "}", single brace pair, exactly {intent,text} keys, valid JSON. SPEC explicitly requires this to be accepted.

descr: Valid envelope followed only by a single trailing newline.
rationale: Trailing \n is stripped by trimmingCharacters(.whitespacesAndNewlines); nothing else in the raw string is problematic. SPEC's explicit 'valid object with a trailing newline' acceptance case.

descr: Valid envelope with both leading (tab, newline) and trailing (newline, tab) ordinary whitespace.
rationale: Symmetric whitespace padding on both sides is fully removed by the trim step before the brace/key checks run; no reservedScalars present. Should be accepted per SPEC.

descr: Valid envelope followed by a single U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE (a non-ASCII whitespace character, Unicode category Zs).
rationale: U+3000 is category Zs and is included in Swift's CharacterSet.whitespacesAndNewlines, so it is trimmed away in step 4; it is not in the reservedScalars list (which covers only C0/C1 controls, zero-width, and bidi marks) so step 2 does not flag it either. This is a boundary case distinguishing legitimate non-ASCII whitespace from the BOM/zero-width attack family.

descr: BOM both as the raw prefix AND embedded again inside the "text" value ("hell"+BOM+"o") in the same payload.
rationale: Step 1 already fires on the leading BOM (.forbiddenBOM) before the second occurrence is ever reached; confirms the check order is stable and a single verdict is produced even with multiple BOM occurrences at different structural positions.

descr: BOM is NOT the first character — it's sandwiched between leading and trailing ASCII spaces, before the valid JSON object: two spaces, BOM, two spaces, then the object.
rationale: raw.hasPrefix("﻿") is FALSE here since the first character is a space, so step 1 does NOT catch this — it must be caught by step 2's whole-raw reservedScalar scan (FEFF is listed) which fires regardless of surrounding whitespace, yielding .forbiddenUnicode. This specifically tests that a BOM merely 'near' the start (not literally first) isn't missed by an implementation that only checks the true prefix.

descr: Duplicate "intent" key (second value differs)
rationale: RFC 8259 leaves duplicate object member names parser-dependent; step 7 uses JSONSerialization to compute the key set while step 8 uses a separately-invoked JSONDecoder — two independent JSON parses of the same bytes with no guarantee they resolve the duplicate the same way. A fail-closed strict parser must treat any duplicate top-level key as malformed rather than rely on both parsers agreeing on 'last value wins', since disagreement would let step 7's validated content diverge from step 8's decoded content (classic parser-differential smuggling).

descr: Duplicate "text" key smuggling a second value
rationale: Same duplicate-key ambiguity as above applied to 'text': the visible/validated text and the ultimately-decoded text could differ across the two independent parses (JSONSerialization at step 7 vs JSONDecoder at step 8), so a correct fail-closed parser rejects any repeated top-level key outright rather than trusting last-wins semantics.

descr: Extra unexpected top-level key "extra" alongside valid intent/text
rationale: Contract: only {intent,text} allowed as top-level keys; any additional key must be rejected as missingOrExtraFields regardless of its value, since step 7's key-set equality check is exact-match, not subset/superset.

descr: Missing required "text" key, only "intent" present
rationale: Contract requires both intent and text present; key set {intent} != {intent,text} so step 7 rejects as missingOrExtraFields. LLMEnvelope's lenient decode (?? "") never gets a chance to paper over this because the key-set gate runs before JSONDecoder.

descr: Missing required "intent" key, only "text" present
rationale: Symmetric to the missing-text case: key set {text} != {intent,text}, must reject at step 7 as missingOrExtraFields before decoding is ever attempted.

descr: intent value is JSON null instead of a string
rationale: Contract: MUST ACCEPT only 'both string' values for intent/text. JSON null is present so the key SET check at step 7 still sees exactly {intent,text} and would pass that gate, but LLMEnvelope.intent is typed String — decoding null into a non-optional String must fail. A correct implementation must not let the lenient `decodeIfPresent ?? default` swallow an explicit null into a silent default; that would let a caller inject null to force fallback intent semantics. Expected verdict: reject (malformedEnvelope / wrong type), not silent substitution.

descr: text value is JSON null instead of a string
rationale: Same reasoning as null intent: contract mandates text be a string; a null value must not be silently coerced to empty string by lenient decoding — a correct fail-closed parser rejects explicit null for a required string field rather than defaulting it.

descr: intent value is a JSON number (123) instead of a string
rationale: LLMEnvelope.intent is typed as String; JSONDecoder throws a type-mismatch DecodingError when asked to decode a String from a JSON number, which the parser maps to .malformedEnvelope. Contract explicitly requires both values be strings, so reject is correct.

descr: text value is a JSON boolean (true) instead of a string
rationale: text is typed String in LLMEnvelope; decoding a Bool where a String is expected throws a type-mismatch error at step 8, mapped to .malformedEnvelope. Contract requires string values only, so reject is correct.

descr: text value is a nested JSON object {"a":"b"} instead of a string
rationale: Two independent reasons to reject: (a) step 5's brace count is taken over the WHOLE trimmed string including inside values, and this raw string contains two '{' and two '}' (outer envelope + nested object), so openCount==2 fails the ==1 check and it is rejected at step 5 as malformedEnvelope before JSON parsing even happens; (b) even if brace-counting were value-aware, LLMEnvelope.text is String-typed so decoding a nested object into it would throw a type mismatch at step 8. Either path lands on reject, matching the contract's 'both string' requirement.

descr: Empty JSON object with no keys at all
rationale: Key set {} does not equal the required {intent,text}; step 7's exact key-set comparison fails and the parser must report missingOrExtraFields. This also fails the higher-level contract that both intent and text are mandatory.

descr: Input consisting solely of whitespace (spaces, tab, newline), no JSON object at all
rationale: After trimmingCharacters(.whitespacesAndNewlines) the trimmed string is empty; trimmed.first is nil so the guard 'trimmed.first == "{" && trimmed.last == "}"' fails, producing .malformedEnvelope. There is no object to validate, so reject is unambiguously correct.

descr: Trailing comma after the last member before the closing brace
rationale: Strict JSON grammar (RFC 8259) forbids a trailing comma before '}'; JSONSerialization (which is a strict, standards-conforming parser) fails to parse this at step 7, and the contract only promises acceptance of 'a single well-formed JSON object' — this is not well-formed, so reject is correct.

descr: Single-quoted keys and values (not valid JSON string delimiters)
rationale: JSON strings must use double quotes; single quotes are not valid JSON syntax at all, so JSONSerialization.jsonObject fails to parse the input at step 7 (no valid top-level object can be produced), yielding rejection. Also note braces/quote characters here are plain ASCII so no homoglyph or Unicode reservation applies — this is rejected purely for being invalid JSON, matching the contract's well-formed-JSON requirement.

descr: JavaScript-style line comment ("//") injected between members, not valid in JSON
rationale: JSON has no comment syntax; the '//' sequence produces an invalid token sequence at the location of a JSON value/key, so JSONSerialization fails to parse -> reject. This also probes whether a naive line-based sanitizer might strip 'comments' and accidentally accept smuggled content; the contract only accepts well-formed JSON, and this raw string is not well-formed JSON as given, so it must be rejected as-is.

descr: Extra key "Intent" (capital I) alongside the correct lowercase "intent" and "text"
rationale: JSON object keys are case-sensitive strings; {intent, Intent, text} is a 3-element key set, not equal to the required {intent,text}, so step 7's exact-match check fails as missingOrExtraFields — the presence of a case-variant of an allowed key does not satisfy the exact key-set requirement.

descr: Legitimate envelope with keys in reversed order (text before intent) — order must not matter for set equality
rationale: JSON objects are unordered maps; step 7 compares the KEY SET (not key order) against {intent,text}. Both required keys are present exactly once with no extras, and both values are valid JSON strings, so this must be accepted — a parser that rejected this due to physical key order would be a false-reject bug on ordinary, contract-compliant LLM output.

descr: Legitimate pretty-printed envelope using \r\n and \t whitespace, with full-width Chinese punctuation (，！：（）。) INSIDE the text string value
rationale: Contract SPEC §3.3 rule 4 explicitly requires acceptance of pretty-printing with \t \n \r whitespace AND normal full-width Chinese punctuation inside string VALUES. The full-width punctuation here (，！：（）。) is inside the text string, not in the structural/outside-string positions that trigger the structuralHomoglyph check (which only scans outside JSON string literals), and none of the reservedScalars (control/zero-width/bidi) are present. Key set is exactly {intent,text}, both string-valued, single object, no BOM, no backticks, brace count is 1/1. This must be accepted; rejecting it would be a false-reject blocking normal richly-punctuated Chinese dictation output.

descr: 全形中文標點在字串值內（逗號、句號）
rationale: SPEC §3.3 規則4明確要求接受字串值內的全形中文標點（，。等），且這些字元不在 reservedScalar 或 structuralHomoglyph 清單中（後者只掃描字串外）。

descr: 字串值內含 ASCII 大括號（程式碼片段）
rationale: SPEC 要求接受值內含 ASCII 大括號/引號的一般文字（如程式碼）；這是合法單一 JSON 物件，只是文字內容剛好含 { }。

descr: 字串值內含跳脫雙引號（引述句）
rationale: 值內的雙引號已用反斜線正確跳脫，是合法 JSON 字串；SPEC 明確列出此類輸入必須接受。

descr: 字串值內混用單引號與跳脫雙引號
rationale: 單引號無須跳脫，雙引號已正確跳脫；為常見英文引述文字，SPEC 要求接受。

descr: 字串值內含 \n 換行跳脫（多行內容）
rationale: \n 是合法 JSON 字串跳脫序列，解碼後為換行字元 0x0A，屬於 reservedScalar 的例外（\t \n \r 皆排除），SPEC 明確要求接受多行文字。

descr: 字串值內含 emoji
rationale: emoji 為一般 Unicode 標量，不在 reservedScalar／structuralHomoglyph 清單中，SPEC 要求接受一般口語聽寫內容。

descr: 字串值內混合中英文與數字、百分比
rationale: 混合 CJK/拉丁字母/數字/符號是常見聽寫內容，無 reserved 或 homoglyph 字元，必須接受。

descr: 字串值本身是問句（含全形問號）
rationale: 全形問號屬合法中文標點，SPEC 明確列出「text that is itself a question」為必須接受的合法案例。

descr: 極長字串值（多次重複中文句子）
rationale: 長度本身不是拒絕條件，SPEC 要求接受「very long text」；內容全為合法字元，結構仍是單一合法 JSON 物件。

descr: 字串值以全形驚嘆號結尾
rationale: SPEC 明確列出「text ending in punctuation」必須接受，全形驚嘆號為合法中文標點。

descr: 美化格式 JSON（結構外含 tab／換行縮排）
rationale: SPEC 明確要求接受 pretty-printed JSON，結構外的 \t \n \r 屬 reservedScalar 例外；trimmingCharacters 後仍以 { 開頭 } 結尾，且大括號各恰一個。

descr: JSON 物件鍵順序顛倒（text 在前、intent 在後）
rationale: JSONSerialization/JSONDecoder 及 SPEC 皆未要求鍵順序；topLevelKeys 是集合比較（== {intent,text}），只要恰好兩鍵齊全即應接受。

descr: 字串值內描述 JSON 格式（跳脫大括號與引號）
rationale: 值內的大括號與引號皆在字串內部且引號已正確跳脫；這是完全合法、常見（描述程式碼／API）的聽寫或編輯內容，SPEC 要求接受含 ASCII 大括號/引號的一般文字。

descr: 字串值內含跳脫反斜線（Windows 路徑）
rationale: 反斜線已用 \\ 正確跳脫為合法 JSON 字串，內容為常見口語聽寫（描述檔案路徑），不含任何 reserved 或 homoglyph 字元。

descr: 字串值內含全形冒號與全形括號（地址）
rationale: 全形冒號／括號在字串值內部，不受 structuralHomoglyph 規則影響（該規則只掃描字串外），SPEC §3.3 規則4明確允許值內全形標點。

descr: 字串值內含 \t 定位字元（表格欄位分隔）
rationale: \t 解碼後為 0x09，屬 reservedScalar 例外（\t \n \r 排除），常見於表格式聽寫內容，必須接受。

descr: 字串值內含多組 ASCII 大括號（類程式碼條件敘述）
rationale: 值內三組 { } 皆為文字內容的一部分而非 JSON 結構；SPEC 要求接受含 ASCII 大括號的一般文字，結構層面仍只有最外層一個物件。

descr: 字串值內同時含程式碼引號與大括號混合（複合案例）
rationale: 綜合案例：單引號、ASCII 大括號、跳脫雙引號、全形句號同時出現在字串值內，皆為合法字元組合且不影響最外層 JSON 結構（仍是一個物件、一對最外層大括號）。
